- <a id="inv-txn.atomic"></a>**`txn.atomic`** · transactions — A rolled-back or failed transaction leaves no effect.
- <a id="inv-txn.bank_conserved"></a>**`txn.bank_conserved`** · transactions — Concurrent transfers preserve the total.
- <a id="inv-txn.constraints_under_race"></a>**`txn.constraints_under_race`** · transactions — Unique and foreign keys hold under concurrent writers.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_circular_info"></a>**`txn.no_circular_info`** · transactions — G1c: no cycle of transactions each seeing the other's writes.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_dirty_read"></a>**`txn.no_dirty_read`** · transactions — G1a and G1b: no transaction reads uncommitted or aborted data.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_dirty_write"></a>**`txn.no_dirty_write`** · transactions — G0: no write overwrites another transaction's uncommitted write.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_lost_update"></a>**`txn.no_lost_update`** · transactions — P4: a committed update is never overwritten by a stale read-modify-write.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_read_skew"></a>**`txn.no_read_skew`** · transactions — G-single: repeatable read and above read one snapshot.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_write_skew"></a>**`txn.no_write_skew`** · transactions — G2-item: serializable prevents write skew.
- <a id="inv-txn.visible_after_commit"></a>**`txn.visible_after_commit`** · transactions — After COMMIT returns, every new transaction sees its writes.

## Exemptions and refusals

Each ☑️ and ⛔, with the reason and the test that proves it.

- `doltgres.main` × `txn.no_read_skew`: exempt. The claim is about repeatable read and serializable. The Doltgres docs (concepts/sql/transaction) say Doltgres uses the Read Committed transaction model, so it must refuse both levels when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.main/txn.no_read_skew`.
- `doltgres.main` × `txn.no_write_skew`: exempt. The claim is about serializable, which the Doltgres docs say Doltgres does not offer, so it must refuse it when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.main/txn.no_write_skew`.
- `doltgres.release` × `txn.no_read_skew`: exempt. The claim is about repeatable read and serializable. The Doltgres docs (concepts/sql/transaction) say Doltgres uses the Read Committed transaction model, so it must refuse both levels when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.release/txn.no_read_skew`.
- `doltgres.release` × `txn.no_write_skew`: exempt. The claim is about serializable, which the Doltgres docs say Doltgres does not offer, so it must refuse it when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.release/txn.no_write_skew`.
- `doltgres.main` × `txn.isolation`, 2 members: unsupported. The Doltgres docs (concepts/sql/transaction): Doltgres uses the Read Committed transaction model. Requesting this level must be refused, not silently run at another. Members: `repeatable read`, `serializable`. Each is proven by its own test (`proven_by` in the subject's file).
- `doltgres.release` × `txn.isolation`, 2 members: unsupported. The Doltgres docs (concepts/sql/transaction): Doltgres uses the Read Committed transaction model. Requesting this level must be refused, not silently run at another. Members: `repeatable read`, `serializable`. Each is proven by its own test (`proven_by` in the subject's file).
